title: Your Embedding Model Is SMARTer Than You Think
claim: Single-vector retrieval pools away local evidence and returns wrong candidates; late interaction over existing hidden states recovers fine-grained matches without retraining.
layout: 3 panels: single-vector top-left, ours right with zoom-in, hybrid scoring bottom-left
description: A query bar sits across the top: a question about regulatory frameworks, with two regions highlighted in blue boxes. Beneath it, the left panel (red border) shows single-vector retrieval. Five top-ranked document thumbnails are marked with green checks and red crosses (2 correct, 3 wrong). Below them, a confused robot, query and candidate embedding models, and rows of gray token boxes feeding a single pink pooled vector. A trash can marks the discarded tokens. The right panel (green border) shows the SMART adaptation. Its top-5 ranking has three checks and two crosses. A yellow zoom-in connects the last hit to a scatter plot of GDP per capita against operational efficiency. Dashed blue lines link the highlighted query phrases to matching legend entries. At the bottom left, a green-bordered panel shows a robot with a lightbulb. It illustrates SMART hybrid scoring, with late-interaction arcs between pink token states of query and candidate.
caption: Standard single-vector embedding models (Qwen3-VL-Embedding-8B in this figure) compress sequences into single token representations, which often results in losing local information and underutilizing the remaining hidden states. While existing multi-vector approaches require expensive retraining, SMART shows empirically that the hidden states of single-vector embedders are already geometrically aligned for local matching. SMART thus transforms any single-vector model into a multi-vector variant both during inference and via lightweight post-training, the former improving with no training, and the latter saving time and rivaling SoTA multi-vector embedders.
abstract: Multimodal retrieval relies heavily on single-vector retrievers, which compress rich, sequential token sequences into one single global representation. While efficient, they discard fine-grained, local evidence critical for dense retrieval tasks. Multi-vector approaches were introduced as a solution, but they strictly require training and many ignore the necessity of a globally summarizing representation. To address this, we introduce SMART, a framework that unlocks the latent multi-vector capabilities of standard single-vector models. We first observe that gradients from the pooled contrastive objective reach the preceding hidden states, and then show empirically that these states are already organized for cosine-based matching. By applying direct late-interaction over these frozen hidden states during inference, SMART acts as a plug-and-play upgrade that consistently improves performance across diverse modalities, improving even the state-of-the-art models further on MMEB-V2. We also show that lightweight post-training saves time and compute while further improving Visual Document retrieval, allowing a single-vector model to perform competitively with SoTA multi-vector counterparts. SMART targets dense retrieval: its gains concentrate on fine-grained and visual-document tasks, it is on par on global tasks such as classification, and it trades additional per-token index storage for these gains. Ultimately, SMART offers both a highly efficient inference enhancement and a powerful finetuning technique for multimodal retrieval. We open source our code and weights at https://github.com/HanSolo9682/SMART.
